run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T13:06:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because a small but nonzero fraction of requests handled by frontend-proxy's 'ingress' server span are answered with HTTP 503. At the alert's own timestamp 13:06:53Z, the ERROR-status ingress span rate is exactly 0.011111111111111112 spans/s (12.437/s UNSET), which reproduces the alert annotation's 'current' value, so the alert (condition: rate > 0) is driven by these 503s. The 503s are not frontend-proxy application errors: its Envoy access log records them as '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the upstream cluster 'frontend', and each failing ingress span is paired with a 'router frontend egress' client span carrying error=true and http.status_code=0 (no HTTP response received). The failed requests produce no frontend server span; the frontend service itself shows no error spans over the window, its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, memory is ~123-127 MB against a 200Mi limit, and the single service endpoint matches that pod. So the proximate cause of the alert is upstream connection termination on the frontend-proxy -> frontend hop. Why the frontend closes those connections is not established: the frontend container returned no application log lines, its Node/keep-alive settings and frontend-proxy's upstream connection settings are not readable in this Run, and no error appears in frontend's own telemetry. The frontend container is CPU-constrained (100m limit, ~32% of CFS periods throttled, ~0.052 cores used), which is a plausible aggravating factor but only a correlation. The failure share is tiny (~0.089% of ingress spans at 13:06:53), but it is nonzero for the whole measured window (12:42-13:22), so the '> 0' alert stays firing.

claims.text: At the alert timestamp 13:06:53Z the ERROR-status 'ingress' span rate of service frontend-proxy is 0.011111111111111112 per second, and STATUS_CODE_UNSET is 12.437037037037037 per second; the alert annotation's 'current: 0.01111111111111111' therefore equals the error-span rate, not an error percentage.

Same instant, ERROR spans are only ~0.089% of frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans (ratio 0.0008925914906277895), i.e. about 4 failed requests in the preceding 5 minutes out of ~12.4 requests/s: the alert is 'above 0', so this sparse failure is enough to keep it firing.

frontend-proxy has only two span operations: server span 'ingress' and client span 'router frontend egress'; their status labels are ERROR and UNSET, and error-span counts rise with traffic through the window (increase over 600s peaks at ~8.42 for ingress ERROR around 13:01-13:03, ~9.2 over 1231s later).

frontend-proxy's Envoy access log records the failures as '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with upstream cluster 'frontend', observed at 13:05:30, 13:05:41, 13:06:14, 13:06:42, 13:08:10 and 13:16:47 (e.g. GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, GET /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars, GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4, POST /api/checkout).

In the error-tagged trace sample, all 8 frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with recorded error carry http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR, and each is paired with a 'router frontend egress' client span carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0" (no HTTP response), while 3 ingress spans in the same sample returned http.status_code=200.

Whole trace 006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c contains 4 spans only: load-generator 'user_browse_product' -> load-generator 'GET' (503, error) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (503, error) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error, http.status_code 0); no frontend span exists in it, so the request never completed at the frontend.

The service that answered the failing callers is not returning its own errors: across the window every one of frontend's 14 span operations has 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans (including GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct), while frontend-proxy accumulates 11.28 error spans in the same 1231s increase.

frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t (owner ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq are both Running and Ready with restartCount 0, state running, no lastState.terminated, and both Deployments report 1/1 ready/available with NewReplicaSetAvailable at 12:27:55Z / 12:27:57Z.
The Service 'frontend' has exactly one endpoint, 100.96.4.88 on node i-029c97e90b3730286 targeting pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t, so the 503s are not explained by a stale or empty endpoint list.

The frontend container is CPU-constrained: limit 100m / request 50m, usage ~0.052-0.055 cores, and ~32% of its CFS periods are throttled steadily across the window; frontend-proxy (limit 30m) is throttled ~6.5% of periods at ~0.014 cores.

The frontend container's memory working set is 123-127 MB, below its 200Mi limit, and its pod has no memory-driven termination; the node hosting both pods (i-029c97e90b3730286) is Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False.

Every pod in otel-demo (22 pods, including frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator and otel-collector) was created at 12:27:55-12:30:02Z, about 39 minutes before the alert started at 13:06:53Z; the 503 failures continue well after that (last observed failure 13:16:47Z) with no restarts in either pod.

The other services with error spans in the same window carry only flagd streaming client spans (ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.05, fraud-detection 4.10, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.05 per 1231s); none of them is a request-failure error tied to frontend-proxy's 503s.

The callers that received the failures are visible in the sample: 8 load-generator 'GET' spans carry error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR, one per failed frontend-proxy ingress span.

Likely mechanism for the 503s: frontend-proxy (Envoy) reuses keep-alive connections to the frontend, and the upstream terminates a connection before response headers (Envoy detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}'), e.g. the Node.js frontend closing idle keep-alive connections while Envoy dispatches a request on one. Envoy's exact diagnostic and the absence of any frontend error span support this, but the frontend's Node keep-alive timeouts and frontend-proxy's upstream connection settings are not readable in this Run, so the mechanism is not proven.

A contributing factor may be CPU starvation on the frontend pod (100m CPU limit, ~32% of CFS periods throttled, ~0.052 cores used while serving ~10-12 requests/s): throttled event-loop scheduling can delay connection handling and widen the window for connection-close races. This is only a correlation; no evidence directly ties a throttling spike to any individual 503.

Rejected: the frontend application returning 5xx errors. frontend has 0 error spans in all 14 of its operations, and the failing trace contains no frontend span at all, so the caller never received an application error response.

Rejected: a frontend crash, OOM kill or restart causing the failures. restartCount is 0 with no lastState.terminated, the container uses ~123-127 MB of a 200Mi limit, and its pod has been Ready continuously since 12:27:55Z.

Rejected: the alert being a leftover of the 12:27:55Z rollout of the otel-demo workloads. The alert started at 13:06:53Z, 39 minutes after the rollout, the two pods have restarted 0 times, and 'UC ... connection_termination' failures are still logged at 13:08:10Z and 13:16:47Z.

Against a frontend-proxy-internal fault: frontend-proxy itself is healthy at the pod level (Ready, restartCount 0), only ~6.5% of its CFS periods are throttled, and every failure is reported by Envoy as an upstream-side connection termination with http.status_code=0 on the egress span, i.e. the failure is on the outbound 'frontend' hop, not a local response the proxy generated.

Inspect and align the connection-close settings on the frontend-proxy -> frontend hop: the frontend's Node.js server keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout versus frontend-proxy's upstream HTTP keepalive/idle timeouts (or disable upstream connection reuse for the 'frontend' cluster) and confirm whether 'UC ... connection_termination' disappears.

Consider raising the frontend container's 100m CPU limit/request (it is throttled ~32% of periods while serving the current load) and adding readiness probes to frontend and frontend-proxy, since neither container currently declares a readiness or liveness probe, so an unhealthy instance would stay in the Service endpoints.

gaps: No frontend application log lines were returned for 12:55-13:20Z (0 lines read), so the frontend's own view of why it closed the upstream connections is unknown.

The frontend's Node.js HTTP keep-alive/header timeout settings and frontend-proxy's upstream connection/keepalive configuration could not be read: no frontend or frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in otel-demo (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, product-catalog-products), and the settings are baked into the container images.

The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' is not present in this Prometheus's rule list (rule_name query returned no_data; alert rules with severity=warning also returned nothing), so the exact alert expression and evaluation window cannot be verified; the observed ingress ERROR span rate at 13:06:53Z matches the alert value exactly.
Span-metric data starts around 12:42Z, so whether these 503s existed before that (e.g. before the alert's 13:06:53Z start) and what the pre-window baseline was is unknown.
The NetworkPolicy check returned no data, so the absence of network policies (and the network configuration at incident time) cannot be asserted; only current cluster state was observable.

failed requests leave no frontend span (and no frontend log), so it is unknown which frontend code path or connection was terminated; whether the termination originated in the frontend process or elsewhere on the pod network cannot be distinguished from the available data.
Kubernetes objects are the state at query time, not during the incident window, so pod/deployment/endpoint configuration at 13:06:53Z cannot be proven.
The change history integration is not available, so whether a configuration change touched frontend/frontend-proxy around the alert onset could not be checked.
next_steps: Pull the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule configuration to confirm the intended expression (the observed value equals the ERROR ingress-span rate in spans/s) and consider requiring a sustained failure threshold instead of '> 0'.

Verify the frontend Node.js keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout values against frontend-proxy's upstream keepalive and idle timeouts, and test disabling upstream connection reuse for the 'frontend' cluster.

Retain/review frontend stdout logs and, if available, longer-retention span metrics to determine when the 'UC connection_termination' failures first appeared and whether they correlate with traffic volume.

Review frontend CPU limit (100m) against the ~10-12 requests/s it serves and its ~32% CFS throttling; add readiness/liveness probes to frontend and frontend-proxy so unhealthy instances leave the Service endpoints.
